defects.description: The use of 'bisect_left(ids, cursor)' violates the 'exclusive' contract defined in the docstring. 'bisect_left' returns the index of the first occurrence of the cursor. Starting the window at this index includes the item the caller already received, resulting in duplicate items across pages.

Creating the 'ids' list via comprehension '[it["id"] for it in items]' is an O(N) operation. This negates the performance benefit of keyset pagination (which should be O(log N) or O(1)) and will cause high latency and memory usage for large datasets.

Accessing 'window[-1]["id"]' assumes the item is a dictionary. If 'items' contains objects, this will raise a TypeError. Furthermore, the function does not check if 'id' exists, potentially raising a KeyError.
The docstring claims to return a 'slice', but the function returns a materialized list (the window). In Python, 'slice' typically refers to the slice object itself.

obvious_bugs: Off-by-one error where the cursor item is included in the next page results
O(N) full scan of the items list to extract IDs on every pagination call
notes: The implementation correctly handles the terminal 'None' cursor case, but the fundamental logic for skipping the cursor is incorrect (should use 'bisect_right' or 'bisect_left + 1') and the performance is poor for an in-memory utility.
